text: Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics grounds virtue in eudaimonia and defines each virtue as a mean between extremes; courage sits between cowardice and recklessness, and the doctrine of the mean is what distinguishes his account from later deontic or consequentialist formulations.

aristotle nicomachean ethics eudaimonia mean courage cowardice recklessness

street evolutionary debunking realism constructivism reflective equilibrium

text: Finished a careful rereading of Kant's Groundwork this month; the universalisability formulation and the humanity formulation came apart more cleanly than I'd remembered from undergrad and I can now state where the contradiction-in-conception tests actually bite.

kant groundwork universalisability humanity contradiction conception reread
